clue.text: Oil-producing nation

indicators.note: producing suggests the word nation is worked up into something new, a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A country that pumps out petroleum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil-producing nation' reads as one phrase about a petrostate, but 'Oil' is the definition, a verb, and 'producing' tells you to rearrange NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: To anoint someone is to smear oil on them in a ceremony, so the verb oil fits.

clue.text: Safe bet, said plausible gangster

indicators.note: said tells us the word for plausible is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: something plausible is likely
a hood, short for hoodlum, is a gangster

explanation.surface: Someone calls a credible mobster a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' applies only to the word for 'plausible': LIKELY, spoken, gives LIKELI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a high probability is close to a certainty, so a safe bet loosely means a strong probability.

clue.text: Wife greeting snoring youngster, a remarkable person

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
ZZ is the cartoon sound of snoring
a kid is a youngster

explanation.surface: A wife greets a sleeping child, who turns out to be exceptional.
explanation.definitionFit: A prodigy who is unusually gifted, especially when young, is an outstanding individual.

clue.text: Besotted with acting, claims a bit of talent

indicators.note: claims means the word for acting takes the next piece into itself

parts.note: doing, as in what you are doing, means acting

indicators.note: a bit of picks out just the first letter of the word talent

explanation.surface: Someone infatuated with performing insists they have a little ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Being besotted means being foolishly infatuated, the same as fondly adoring someone to excess.

clue.text: Maybe some lads like old-fashioned girls

indicators.note: maybe hints that the words some lads could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Perhaps a few boys fancy girls of the traditional sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Damosel is an archaic form of damsel, a young unmarried woman, so it suits girls described as old-fashioned.

clue.text: Taking pains done with circulating job centre

indicators.note: circulating means the word for done goes round the next piece

parts.note: if you are through, you are done or finished

indicators.note: centre picks out the middle letter of the word job

explanation.surface: Someone diligent finishes their visit to an employment office.
explanation.walkthrough: A job centre is a British state employment office; here 'job centre' just gives O, the middle of JOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A painstaking person is meticulous, leaving nothing out, which is what taking pains describes.

clue.text: Inwardly unfeeling, succumbs to those that won't be moved

indicators.note: inwardly means the next word's synonym sits inside the word for succumbs

parts.note: to succumb can mean to die
a hard person is unfeeling

explanation.surface: Someone cold at heart gives way to stubborn opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn people who refuse to change their views are resistant to persuasion and stand firm.

clue.text: First boys to enter when teacher's around could be spare

indicators.note: to enter means the first piece goes into the reversed title
around means the word for teacher is turned back to front

parts.note: sir is what pupils call a male teacher; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: first picks out the initial letter of the word boys

explanation.surface: The first boys come in while the teacher is about, with time to kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns SIR into RIS; 'to enter' puts B inside. 'Spare' as in spare ribs, a cut of pork.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare ribs are a cut of pork from the ribcage, so the bones could be described as spare.

clue.text: Cast of beginners to study hard, exercising daily

indicators.note: beginners means the opening letters of the following four words

explanation.surface: A theatre company of novices must study and exercise hard each day.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something, as a snake does its skin, is to cast it off.

clue.text: For such short-sightedness I pay more outrageously — not again!

indicators.note: outrageously suggests wild treatment of the letters, so they are rearranged
not tells us the letters for again are taken away

parts.note: re is a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Someone complains that paying extra for poor eyesight is outrageous and won't happen twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not again' removes RE from MORE, leaving MO; 'outrageously' then mixes I, PAY and MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is the medical term for being unable to see distant things clearly.

clue.text: Pretty big: when carrying drug can be taken by force

indicators.note: carrying means the word for pretty big holds the next piece

parts.note: sizable means fairly large
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A large consignment of drugs may be confiscated by police.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seizable is able to be grabbed or confiscated, which is being taken by force.

clue.text: Distinguished detective being sweet

parts.note: spotted means noticed or picked out, so distinguished
a dick is slang for a detective

explanation.surface: An eminent private eye is a lovely person.
explanation.walkthrough: SPOTTED DICK is a British steamed suet pudding with currants.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet in British English is a dessert, and this suet pudding with dried fruit is one.

clue.text: Shabby dog's two orders?

parts.note: one command to a dog is to lie flat
another command tells a dog to walk close beside its owner

explanation.surface: A scruffy hound is given a couple of instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoes worn down at the back look scruffy, so the phrase means looking poor and neglected.

clue.text: PS And I've managed to be afflicted with a swelling in a leg joint

definitions.text: afflicted with a swelling in a leg joint

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters are handled and arranged anew

explanation.surface: A postscript says that someone has got by with a swollen knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Spavin is a disease of a horse's hock causing swelling, so a spavined horse suffers from it.

clue.text: Poor man admits late starter's affable

indicators.note: admits means the word for poor man lets the next piece in

parts.note: a peasant is a poor farm labourer

indicators.note: starter means the opening letter of the word late

explanation.surface: An impoverished man agrees that the person who arrived late is friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: An affable person is friendly and agreeable, which is what a pleasant person is.

clue.text: Welsh go dancing the cancan?

indicators.note: dancing hints that the letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: Would a Welshman step out in a high-kicking French dance?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark says the cancan is an example: a show of kicking legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg show is a revue featuring dancers showing off their legs, and the cancan is such a display.

clue.text: Historic town, lice infection over, guarded by witches

indicators.note: guarded by means the reversed piece sits inside the word for witches

parts.note: hags are ugly old women or witches

indicators.note: over means the word for lice infection is turned around

parts.note: nits are the eggs of lice, a common infestation

explanation.surface: An old town with a plague of lice is kept safe by witches.
explanation.walkthrough: The town in East Sussex is famous for the battle of 1066; 'lice infection' points to the eggs, not the insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings gave its name to the 1066 battle, making it a town of great historical note.

clue.text: Myself with mate following wordy book concerning loving mother

indicators.note: following means the first pieces come after the word book in the answer

parts.note: the OED, Oxford English Dictionary, is a book full of words
I means myself
a pal is a mate

explanation.surface: Someone and their friend, after reading a big dictionary, discuss maternal love.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's complex, named after the Greek king who married his mother, describes desire for one's mother.

clue.text: View racket one way in part of northern Europe

parts.note: to scan is to view
a din is a racket or loud noise
a means one
via is Latin for way

explanation.surface: Seeing a noisy tennis racket in one direction in the north of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The region comprising Norway, Sweden and Denmark is in the north of the continent.

clue.text: Quality of a busy tea urn

indicators.note: busy suggests the letters bustle about into a new order

explanation.surface: The excellence of a well-used café boiler.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature is their essential character or quality.

clue.text: You get ninny turning up with tree from Java

parts.note: U is text-speak for you

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word for ninny is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sap is a fool or ninny

explanation.surface: A fool gets surprised by a tree from Java.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a tree native to Java whose sap was used as an arrow poison.

clue.text: Good man's into first-class wine

indicators.note: into means the abbreviation for the good man goes inside the first-class letters

parts.note: A1 is first-class, written here as AI
St, for saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A saintly man takes to superior wine.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-rate; the figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian white from Piedmont.

clue.text: Constable imbibing 21 down: what did you say about being a mixture?

indicators.note: imbibing means the abbreviation for constable drinks in the wine

parts.note: PC, police constable
the answer to 21 down, a wine

indicators.note: about means the query is turned around

parts.note: eh? is how one asks someone to repeat themselves

explanation.surface: A policeman drinking wine asks for a repeat of something mixed.
explanation.walkthrough: '21 down' is a cross-reference: use that answer, the wine, as the piece the policeman drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a work made of borrowed pieces, a medley or hotchpotch.

clue.text: Some poetry most Anzacs could deliver

indicators.note: could deliver means the words most Anzacs hold the answer and give it up

explanation.surface: Most Australian and New Zealand soldiers could recite verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Anzacs are soldiers of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem, so a portion of verse.

clue.text: Complaint of individuals getting out of hospital

indicators.note: getting means the word for individuals receives the letter inside

parts.note: singles are individual people or items

indicators.note: out of means the first letter is taken from the word hospital

explanation.surface: An illness suffered by single people discharged from hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness, and shingles is a painful viral rash.

clue.text: Believe in tick?

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to believe it
tick is British slang for ..., as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Do you trust a mark of approval?
explanation.definitionFit: To credit is to trust a statement, and buying on credit is buying on tick.
